newsitem.title: USA: SEC to announce settlement on inside trade case.
newsitem.headline: SEC to announce settlement on inside trade case.

text.p: Investor Joseph Cusimano has agreed to pay $1.6 million in penalities to settle civil charges he violated federal securities laws in connection with an insider trading case, an SEC official said Monday.
The Securities and Exchange Commision is expected to make a formal announcement Tuesday, the official said.
Cusimano, one of 17 people charged in an insider trading scheme on four stocks of AT&T takeover targets, agreed to pay $587,659 in prejudgment interest and a $963,341 disgorgement of his profits.
Cusimano also had an additional $1 million civil fine levied against him, but that was waived in view of a $1 million fine that had been levied against him in a criminal case.
District Judge John Sprizzo in the southern district of New York entered the final judgement on January 24 against Cusimano, the SEC said.
The SEC said it charged Cusimano with trading on three of the four stocks from information provided by his friend Charles Brumfield, former vice-president for labor relations at AT&T.
Brumfield is currently serving a 21-month sentence in a federal prison in Wisconsin for his role in orchestrating the trading.

The scheme, which extended from December 1988 to about 1993, is believed to have netted the participants about $2.6 million in illegal profits involving four targets: NCR Corp, Digital Microwave Corp, Paradyne Corp and Teradata Corp.
Two other defendants, Thomas Alger and William Mylett settled with the SEC last week. Litigation against the remaining defendants continues.
